references.text: Zacchaeus climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree to see Jesus, directly because he could not see him due to the crowd and his short stature ([ref:Luk 19:4|Luke 19:4]).
Herod also sought to see Jesus – the verb 'sought to see' (ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν) is the same expression used about Zacchaeus ([ref:Luk 9:9|Luke 9:9]).
Herod had for a long time wanted to see Jesus – again the expression of wanting to see him is used, but with a completely different motive than Zacchaeus ([ref:Luk 23:8|Luke 23:8]).
The Greeks came to Philip and said: "We want to see Jesus." The desire to see Jesus is a recurring theme in the Gospels ([ref:Joh 12:21|John 12:21]).

Without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever comes to God must believe that he exists. Zacchaeus' eagerness to see who Jesus was shows a beginning of faith and seeking after him ([ref:Heb 11:6|Hebrews 11:6]).

The men carrying the paralyzed man could not find any way through the crowd either, and had to find an alternative way to reach Jesus – parallel to Zacchaeus who was hindered by the crowd ([ref:Luk 5:19|Luke 5:19]).
Jesus' mother and brothers could not come to him because of the crowd, a similar motive as in the story of Zacchaeus ([ref:Luk 8:19|Luke 8:19]).
A clear thematic parallel: In both cases there is a situation where a person (the healed man/Zacchaeus) cannot see or know who Jesus is because of circumstances related to the crowd.
